TREC’s 2025 Product Recommendation rubric separates functional substitutes from complements and explicitly distinguishes unknown compatibility from demonstrated incompatibility. This supports auditing product relationship and compatibility separately; similarity alone cannot establish usefulness or redundancy for a particular user. Missing specifications should produce an unknown judgment. [Official track guidelines](https://huggingface.co/datasets/trec-product-search/product-recommendation-2025/discussions/1/files).

Research on evidence sufficiency supports separating uncertainty from rejection. *Sufficient Context* (2024 preprint; ICLR 2025) distinguishes relevant context from information adequate to answer and investigates guided abstention. *Trust or Escalate* (ICLR 2025) evaluates selective judgments against human agreement. These findings support measuring both coverage—the fraction receiving a definite judgment—and error among definite judgments, rather than rewarding confident answers alone. Neither establishes recommendation-specific reliability automatically. [Sufficient Context](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.06037), [Trust or Escalate](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/08dabd5345b37fffcbe335bd578b15a0-Paper-Conference.pdf).

Proposed adaptation: require each usefulness, redundancy, or compatibility judgment to cite supporting spans from available titles, descriptions, or explicitly supplied feedback, with history references and timestamps where relevant. Record relationship, user-specific usefulness, compatibility, and evidence sufficiency separately. Purchases establish historical interaction, not current ownership or fulfilled needs; a substitute is not automatically redundant. Manually annotate recommendations for all twenty sampled users, resolve disagreements, and compare automated judgments with human labels, reporting unknown rates and unsupported-claim rates. Treat this as pilot rubric calibration, not proof of general reliability; preserve macro validation HR@10 as the model-selection criterion.
